findings.evidence: Artin.lean:245-247 `natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic {f} (hf : f ∈ virtualCharacters k G) : Nat.card G • f ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G (fun C ↦ IsCyclic C)` — no hypothesis on `k` beyond `Field`; Ideal.lean:194-195 `indVirtualCharactersBaseChangeRat_surjective (P) (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) (h : ∀ f ∈ virtualCharacters k G, n • f ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P)` — `hn` is a ℕ-statement, so no char-zero input is needed. findings.fix: Replace lines 323-327 with `exact natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic hf` and lines 360-364 with `exact natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isElementary hf`, and drop the now-unused `[CharZero k] [IsAlgClosed k]` from both statements (Artin.lean:317, :354).
findings.issue: After `apply indVirtualCharactersBaseChangeRat_surjective (fun C ↦ IsCyclic C) (Nat.card G) Nat.card_pos.ne'` and `intro f hf`, the goal is exactly `Nat.card G • f ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G (fun C ↦ IsCyclic C)`. Lines 323-326 apply `indVirtualCharacterSpan_le_indVirtualCharacters` and then rewrite back with `← indVirtualCharacters_eq_indVirtualCharacterSpan`, a no-op round trip whose only effect is to require `[IsAlgClosed k]` and `[CharZero k]`, which the theorem then advertises as hypotheses of rational Artin surjectivity. Same pattern at lines 360-363 for the elementary version.

findings.evidence: Artin.lean:256-257 `indVirtualCharacterSpan_le_indVirtualCharacters : indVirtualCharacterSpan k G P ≤ indVirtualCharacters k G P` and Ideal.lean:119-121 `indVirtualCharacters_le_virtualCharacters : indVirtualCharacters k G P ≤ virtualCharacters k G`; grep for `indVirtualCharacterSpan_le_virtualCharacters` across `TauCeti/` returns only its own declaration at Artin.lean:172.
findings.fix: Delete it, or move it below line 256 and prove it as `indVirtualCharacterSpan_le_indVirtualCharacters.trans indVirtualCharacters_le_virtualCharacters`.
findings.issue: `indVirtualCharacterSpan_le_virtualCharacters` re-derives from scratch (via `ofFDRep_eq_ofCharacter` and `ind_ofFDRep_mem_virtualCharacters`) a statement that is the composition of two lemmas the PR already exports, and it has no consumer anywhere in the repo.

summary: The new Möbius/direct-sum/base-change material is genuinely new and reuses located Mathlib and TauCeti API. Two redundancies remain: both rational-surjectivity proofs take a round trip through `indVirtualCharacterSpan` to reach a goal an earlier theorem closes verbatim (dragging in `[CharZero k] [IsAlgClosed k]` that the statements then do not need), and `indVirtualCharacterSpan_le_virtualCharacters` re-derives a composite of two exported lemmas.
